speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to start our assessment, can you describe exactly how the swelling began and what symptoms, like pain or redness, you are experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (specifically Oligoarticular JIA).

The lack of a specific trauma event in an 18-month-old with unilateral knee swelling and a family history strongly suggests an autoimmune etiology rather than an injury. I will proceed with ordering inflammatory markers and imaging to confirm this diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, RF.
REQUEST IMAGES: Right Knee X-Ray.
